# emojis-list

[![Dependency status](http://example.invalid/david/Kikobeats/emojis-list.svg?style=flat-square)](https://example.invalid/Kikobeats/emojis-list)
[![Dev Dependencies Status](http://example.invalid/david/dev/Kikobeats/emojis-list.svg?style=flat-square)](https://example.invalid/Kikobeats/emojis-list#info=devDependencies)
[![NPM Status](http://example.invalid/npm/dm/emojis-list.svg?style=flat-square)](https://example.invalid/package/emojis-list)
[![Donate](https://example.invalid/badge/donate-paypal-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://example.invalid/kikobeats)

> Complete list of standard Unicode Hex Character Code that represent emojis.

**NOTE**: The lists is related with the Unicode Hex Character Code. The representation of the emoji depend of the system. Will be possible that the system don't have all the representations.

## Install

```bash
npm install emojis-list --save
```

If you want to use in the browser (powered by [Browserify](http://example.invalid/)):

```bash
bower install emojis-list --save
```

and later link in your HTML:

```html
<script src="bower_components/emojis-list/dist/emojis-list.js"></script>
```

## Usage

```
var emojis = require('emojis-list');
console.log(emojis[0]);
// => 🀄
```

## Related

* [emojis-unicode](https://example.invalid/Kikobeats/emojis-unicode) – Complete list of standard Unicode codes that represent emojis.
* [emojis-keywords](https://example.invalid/Kikobeats/emojis-keywords) – Complete list of am emoji shortcuts.
* [is-emoji-keyword](https://example.invalid/Kikobeats/is-emoji-keyword) – Check if a word is a emoji shortcut.
* [is-standard-emoji](https://example.invalid/kikobeats/is-standard-emoji) – Simply way to check if a emoji is a standard emoji.
* [trim-emoji](https://example.invalid/Kikobeats/trim-emoji) – Deletes ':' from the begin and the end of an emoji shortcut.
